Merz Aesthetics est un laboratoire inter: Merz Aesthetics is a leading international aesthetic medicine laboratory. For the launch of Ultherapy® Prime, a micro-focused ultrasound (HIFU) technology for skin tightening on the face, neck and body, the brand needed a dedicated landing page designed for the French market, able to carry an international message while speaking directly to local patients and practitioners.
Sur un produit de médecine esthétique, l: For an aesthetic medicine product, the page does not just present an offer: it must establish immediate clinical credibility, reassure a demanding audience and guide users towards a concrete action, finding a practitioner authorised to offer the treatment.
Le premier enjeu était de traduire un di: The first challenge was to turn a scientific, international message (technology, protocols, clinical studies) into an accessible reading journey, without losing the rigour expected for a medical device. Too much technicality pushes patients away; too much simplification weakens credibility with practitioners.
Le second enjeu concernait la conversion: The second challenge was conversion. A pharmaceutical brand does not sell the treatment directly: it must direct users to a partner practitioner. The page therefore had to be structured to lead naturally to that step, without breaking the reading experience.
L'objectif était de créer une page qui t: The goal was to create a page that meets both requirements at once: a product showcase desirable and clear enough for the general public, and a resource serious enough to meet the communication standards of an aesthetic medicine laboratory.
Nous avons construit la page comme un pa: We built the page as a progressive journey, from patient benefit to clinical proof, then to the practitioner search, keeping the premium and reassuring tone expected for this kind of product at every step.
Travail sur la structure et le parcours: Work on the structure and journey
La page a été organisée en blocs modulai: The page was organised into modular blocks: presentation of the benefit (tightening, non-invasive, no downtime), explanation of the protocol, the distinction between face and body uses, then social and clinical proof. Each section answers a question visitors naturally ask before moving on to the next step.
Le localisateur de praticiens a été inté: The practitioner locator was built in as the natural end point of the journey rather than as an isolated link, so that conversion follows on from reading instead of feeling like a sales interruption.
Le design devait porter les codes visuel: The design had to carry Merz Aesthetics' visual codes while staying readable and calming. For a medical product aimed at older and younger audiences alike, the balance between premium aesthetics and functional clarity is decisive: the page must be appealing without ever seeming superficial on a health topic.
Les comparatifs avant/après et les témoi: Before/after comparisons and testimonials were included with a restrained presentation, to support the proof without slipping into an overly promotional register, which is hard to reconcile with medical device communication.
Le travail SEO s'est concentré sur la st: The SEO work focused on the product's semantic structure: the name of the technology, treated areas, benefits and FAQ were organised to clearly answer patients' informational queries in France, while keeping the terminology approved by the brand for this type of device.
La FAQ a été pensée comme un point d'ent: The FAQ was designed as an entry point for specific searches (duration, results, pain, indications), so that the page answers the concrete questions that usually come before the decision to consult a practitioner.

The work had to be precise: not too broad, not too technical, not too conceptual.
Sur une application en beta, le principa: For an app in beta, the main danger is that the page stays too vague. If visitors do not quickly understand what the app is for, who it is designed for and why the beta deserves their attention, they leave. With Nation, we had to reduce this abstraction as much as possible. The positioning had to be understandable from the first seconds.
Un autre point important concernait la c: Another important point was credibility. A beta can quickly give the impression of a fragile project if the page does not carry the product well enough. The site had to send the right signal: yes, the project is in beta, but no, it is not half-baked. On the contrary, it had to feel like an already structured product, with a vision, a world and a clear proposition.
Objectif de la landing page de pré-lance: Goal of the pre-launch landing page
L'objectif était de construire une landi: The goal was to build a beta pre-launch landing page able to capture attention, explain Nation's promise and direct visitors to the most logical action. That action could be a download, a sign-up, following the project or finding out more, but in every case it relies on the same condition: the page must turn curiosity into real interest.
Nous avons donc pensé le site comme un o: So we designed the site as a traction tool. It had to support the beta phase, give the product a real presence and set a premium tone from launch. Le copywriting a été traité avec une log: The copywriting followed a logic of maximum clarity. It had to speak to the startup world, but without needless jargon. The wording had to make the app tangible, explain what it is for and show why Nation's networking can appeal to founders, entrepreneurs and players in the startup ecosystem.
Nous avons cherché à simplifier sans app: We aimed to simplify without impoverishing. The page had to get straight to the point while keeping enough substance to inspire trust. Each section was therefore designed as a step in a persuasion funnel: grab attention, clarify the proposition, show the interface, build a premium perception, then push to action. That structure is what makes a beta landing page perform better than one that is too descriptive or too abstract.
La direction artistique a été travaillée: The art direction was designed to support the technological and premium side of the project. Choosing a darker, more controlled look made the product stand out and gave it a modern feel. For a beta app, this is very useful: the design helps prove the project is already taken seriously.
La structure visuelle a également été si: The visual structure was also simplified to make mobile reading easier. A sharp hero, visual demos, well-ordered blocks and well-placed CTAs. The idea was to keep a frictionless journey, able to convince quickly without overwhelming visitors. On this kind of page, too much information often kills conversion. The right strategy is to clearly order what matters.

Cette cohérence sémantique joue sur deux: This semantic consistency works on two levels. It helps Google understand the nature of the project, and at the same time helps visitors quickly identify what they are looking at. When the page names things accurately, SEO and conversion move forward together. That is exactly what we were after for Nation.
